title_original: Sohn Hyun-lok Talks “The Birds”, Korean Education, Invisible Misfortune and Finding Freedom in Flight
editorial_title_zh: 孙贤禄谈《鸟》、韩国教育、看不见的不幸与在飞行中寻得自由
editorial_excerpt_zh: 孙贤禄谈论《鸟》、韩国学校、代际冲突、鸟的意涵，以及他颇具挑战的18个月剪辑。

{"type": "paragraph", "text": "重返釜山国际电影节对孙贤禄而言有着特别的意义。这位在釜山出生并长大的电影人，2023年携长片首作《那个夏天的谎言》在釜山国际电影节新浪潮单元首映，并在那里获得费比西奖。三年后，他带着第二部长片《鸟》归来，这是一部规模明显更大、野心更强的作品，融合了家庭剧、对韩国教育体制的批判，以及愈发怪异的类型元素。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在釜山接受Asian Movie Pulse采访时，孙贤禄谈到了从首部长片到新作的推进、视角从女儿转向母亲、他对韩国学校与育儿的看法、鸟这一隐喻的起源、与专业演员的合作、漫长的剪辑过程，以及他已完成拍摄的第三部长片——一个规模大幅缩小的项目。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "《我的母亲》正在釜山国际电影节展映", "links": [{"text": "Busan International Film Festival", "url": "https://www.biff.kr/eng/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://asianmoviepulse.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Busan-International-Film-Festival-scaled.jpg", "alt": "第31届釜山国际电影节", "caption": "", "credit": "Asian Movie Pulse", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对孙贤禄来说，连续两部长片在釜山国际电影节首映，必然承载着超出职业认可的情感维度。他在釜山出生并度过青少年时期，这让电影节与他的个人经历紧密相连。因此，首作与第二部作品都在这里被介绍给观众，感觉格外有意义，尽管这两部作品的制作条件几乎天差地别。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《那个夏天的谎言》是在没有重要资金支持、剧组仅约七人的情况下制作的。这些限制意味着孙贤禄在影片如何拍摄上选择相对有限。相比之下，《鸟》获得了资金，让他得以与规模大得多的技术人员和演员团队合作。它仍是一部低成本制作，但资源的增加给了他机会去尝试那些在首作中根本不可能实现的想法。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他希望这种差异在成片中可见。孙贤禄没有试图复制《那个夏天的谎言》的亲密感与局限，而是把第二部长片当作一次机会，去发现他的电影还能成为什么。更大的群像、类型元素、视觉效果以及明显更宽广的叙事，部分都源于这种尝试此前无法尝试之事的愿望。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "查看该片评论", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "https://asianmoviepulse.com/ the-birds-2026-by-sohn-hyun-lok-film-review", "links": [{"text": "https://asianmoviepulse.com/", "url": "https://asianmoviepulse.com/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "与此同时，《鸟》的核心人物直接源自他首部电影提出的问题。《那个夏天的谎言》跟随一名少女，她的行为制造出越来越多的麻烦，但在拍摄过程中，孙贤禄开始思考冲突另一侧的那位母亲。为什么母亲无法理解女儿想要什么？为什么同一个家庭的两个人面对同一处境，却得出完全不同的解释？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《鸟》反转了视角。孙贤禄没有继续跟随陷入困境的女儿，而是想跟随一位试图理解孩子的母亲，而这个孩子的行为越来越超出她的理解。艺玉的处境更加复杂，因为她同时是家长和教师。在家里，她与自己女儿挣扎；在学校，她在职业上要对别人的孩子负责。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这一双重角色也让孙贤禄得以审视韩国成年人看待年轻人的方式。尽管片中一些学生的行为可能显得异常严酷，他并不认为这部电影是对当代青少年的控诉。相反，他更感兴趣的是成年人试图理解和控制他们的那些结构。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在他看来，韩国学校体制传统上要求教师非常严格地管理学生。一个后果是倾向于按简单类别给孩子分类：努力学习的、不努力的，以及行为让成年人难以理解的。孙贤禄希望《鸟》恰恰去冲击这种思维方式。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "片中的学生不能被简化为好孩子和坏孩子。他们拥有不同的性格、欲望和理解周围环境的方式，而成年人常常失败，因为他们试图把简单分类强加于远为复杂的事物之上。尽管孙贤禄认为韩国学校正在逐渐改变，教师也越来越多地试图理解学生而非仅仅控制他们，但那种旧心态仍然可见。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "家长从另一个方向参与着同一体系。孙贤禄并不认为《鸟》中呈现的成年人 simply 不关心自己的孩子，即使他们的行为可能显得冷漠。相反，他指向韩国家长的一种倾向：把子女教育和日常发展的很大一部分托付给学校。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "结果可能是一种奇特的责任转移。家长期待教师和机构去教育、监督和解决问题，而教师本身已经被要求管理大量迥异学生的压力压得喘不过气。因此，片中可见的表面冷漠，与其说源于完全缺乏关心，不如说源于一个责任不断被转交的体系。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "然而，鸟的意象几乎早于成片的其他所有方面。孙贤禄最初大约在十三年前服义务兵役期间萌生了基本构想。军旅生活的种种限制令他沮丧，而距离服役结束又遥遥无期，他就这样看着鸟儿径直飞越环绕他的边界。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他记得自己当时很羡慕它们。它们可以自由地飞过困住他的围栏，于是他生出一个简单的念头：他想变成一只鸟。那个画面最终催生了后来成为《The Birds》的最早版本。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "那个阶段的故事与现在大不相同，但一个核心想法已经存在：学生们在看到鸟之后会从楼上跳下。然而，随着孙贤禄在此后几年里继续思考这个项目，其象征意义逐渐发生了变化。自由与逃离仍是其中一部分，但鸟越来越代表某种不那么令人安心的东西。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他开始思考那些毫无预兆地闯入人们生活的不幸。这类事件往往似乎无法事先辨认，可一旦降临，就能彻底改变周围的一切。孙贤禄最终把鸟变成了正是那种无形、不可预测的灾难的隐喻。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这个想法与汝玉的性格密切相关。她试图通过区分和归类来理解世界，就像教育体系对学生进行分类一样。如果她能给某样东西命名、把它分离出来并放进正确的概念盒子里，也许她就能控制它。而降临在她身上的悲剧，却拒绝按照这些规则运作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "鸟成了某种可能早已环绕在人身边却不可见之物的具象呈现。不幸就在附近，但未必能被辨认，直到它骤然降临的那一刻。《The Birds》由此把一种近乎童年式的自由幻想，变成了某种远为令人不安的东西：一个既与逃离禁锢相关、又与面对无法理解的力量相关的意象。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "孙贤禄也有意改变了自己的选角方式。在《That Summer’s Lie》中，他主要寻找不知名演员，几乎每个角色都进行了试镜。到了第二部长片，他想体验另一种电影制作方式，于是决定更多地与经纪公司代理的成熟职业演员合作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他与饰演汝玉的姜敬宪第一次见面，就立刻让他对这个决定感到安心。他们花了很长时间讨论剧本，孙贤禄发现她早已深入思考过剧本的哲学意涵，包括与“庄周梦蝶”相关的想法。他们对素材的理解很快契合，第一次交谈就异常富有成效。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "其他演员也同样被剧本的奇特性质所吸引。他们的专业经验让制作过程与孙贤禄的处女作不同——后者的大量工作都花在寻找没有既定银幕形象的演员上。有了《The Birds》，他得以更直接地专注于与习惯片场要求的演员一起探索素材。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "后期制作则困难得多。孙贤禄亲自剪辑影片，花了大约一年半时间试图找到它的最终形态。这个过程包括反复改变结构和时长，把版本做得更长或更短，放弃某些做法，偶尔在疲惫到无法看清素材时完全离开剪辑。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "视觉特效让这个过程尤为艰难。有几个段落必须在特效完成之前就组装起来，迫使孙贤禄一边想象镜头中最终会出现什么元素，一边判断它们的节奏。对于一位来自《That Summer’s Lie》那种相对精简制作的电影人来说，剪辑这类素材需要学习一套完全不同的流程。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "更大的挑战在于确定《The Birds》究竟应该成为什么样的电影。孙贤禄知道它需要作为一部类型片运作，因此需要某种节奏和维持悬念的能力。与此同时，他不想让类型的要求压过自己的电影感性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "漫长的剪辑期大部分都用于寻找那个中间地带。过于强调常规类型机制，可能拍出一部不再像他自己作品的电影；而完全倾向他过去的风格，又可能削弱越来越奇异的叙事。最终139分钟的版本，代表了他保留这两种冲动的尝试。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在如此疲惫的后期制作之后，孙贤禄的回应是做了几乎完全相反的事。他没有立即尝试再拍一部《The Birds》那种扩大规模的作品，而是已经用寥寥几位演员拍完了第三部长片。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这一次，他想体验几乎完全独自拍电影。他亲自操作摄影机并录制声音，有意舍弃了让《The Birds》得以实现其野心的较大团队。这个新项目围绕演员和创造力的问题展开，不过孙贤禄尚未透露更多细节。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在第二部长片以扩张为特征之后，这个决定显得尤为契合。《The Birds》让孙贤禄得以与更多人合作、尝试类型、加入视觉特效，并在剪辑室里花一年半时间打磨一个复杂的叙事。他的下一部电影似乎是在尝试发现：当几乎所有那些基础设施都消失时，会发生什么。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "从这个意义上说，孙贤禄的早期生涯已经显现出一位刻意尝试相反方法的电影人，而非安于一种路径。《那个夏天的谎言》诞生于严苛的限制之中，《群鸟》则借助更多资源去探索一个更大的世界，而第三部长片如今自愿回到近乎独自制作的模式。将三者联系起来的，是对那些无法真正理解彼此的人的兴趣，尤其是试图跨越日益艰难的鸿沟进行沟通的成年人与年轻人。", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "heading", "text": "Sohn Hyun-lok Talks “The Birds”, Korean Education, Invisible Misfortune and Finding Freedom in Flight"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Sohn Hyun-lok discusses “The Birds”, Korean schools, generational conflict, the meaning of birds and his challenging 18-month edit."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Returning to the Busan International Film Festival has particular significance for Sohn Hyun-lok. Born and raised in the city, the filmmaker premiered his debut feature “That Summer’s Lie” in BIFF’s New Currents section in 2023, where it received the FIPRESCI Prize. Three years later, he returns with his second feature, “The Birds”, a considerably larger and more ambitious production that combines family drama, criticism of the Korean educational system and increasingly strange genre elements."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Speaking with Asian Movie Pulse in Busan, Sohn discussed the progression from his first feature, shifting the perspective from daughter to mother, his thoughts on Korean schools and parenting, the origins of the bird metaphor, working with professional actors, the lengthy editing process and the radically smaller project he has already shot as his third feature."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "My Mother is screening at Busan International Film Festival", "links": [{"text": "Busan International Film Festival", "url": "https://www.biff.kr/eng/"}]}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://asianmoviepulse.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Busan-International-Film-Festival-scaled.jpg", "alt": "31st Busan International Film Festival", "caption": "", "credit": "Asian Movie Pulse"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "For Sohn, premiering two consecutive features at BIFF inevitably carries an emotional dimension beyond professional recognition. He was born and spent his adolescence in Busan, making the festival closely connected to his own personal history. Having both his debut and sophomore film introduced there consequently feels particularly meaningful, although the circumstances under which the two productions were made could hardly have been more different."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“That Summer’s Lie” was produced without significant financial support and with a crew of only around seven people. The limitations meant that Sohn had relatively few options regarding how the movie could be made. “The Birds”, by contrast, received funding and allowed him to work with a substantially larger group of technicians and actors. It remained a low-budget production, but the increase in resources gave him the opportunity to experiment with ideas that would simply have been impossible on his debut."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "He hopes that difference is visible in the finished film. Rather than attempting to reproduce the intimacy and limitations of “That Summer’s Lie”, Sohn treated the second feature as an opportunity to discover what else his cinema could become. The larger ensemble, genre elements, visual effects and considerably broader narrative all emerged partly from that desire to try things he had not previously been able to attempt."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Check the review of the film"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "https://asianmoviepulse.com/ the-birds-2026-by-sohn-hyun-lok-film-review", "links": [{"text": "https://asianmoviepulse.com/", "url": "https://asianmoviepulse.com/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "At the same time, the central character of “The Birds” developed directly from questions raised by his first film. “That Summer’s Lie” followed a teenage girl whose actions create increasing complications, but while making it Sohn began wondering about the mother on the opposite side of those conflicts. Why did the mother fail to understand what her daughter wanted? Why could two members of the same family look at the same situation and arrive at completely different interpretations?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“The Birds” reverses the viewpoint. Instead of remaining with the troubled daughter, Sohn wanted to follow a mother attempting to comprehend a child whose behavior increasingly escapes her understanding. Ye-ok’s position becomes even more complicated because she is simultaneously a parent and a teacher. At home she struggles with her own daughter, while at school she is professionally responsible for other people’s children."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "This dual role also allowed Sohn to examine the way Korean adults look at young people. Although the behavior of some students in the movie can appear exceptionally harsh, he does not regard the film as an accusation against contemporary teenagers. Instead, he is more interested in the structures through which adults attempt to understand and control them."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "In his view, the Korean school system has traditionally required teachers to manage students very strictly. One consequence is the temptation to classify children according to simple categories: those who study hard, those who do not, and those whose behavior adults find difficult to comprehend. Sohn wanted “The Birds” to push against precisely that way of thinking."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The students in the movie cannot be reduced to good and bad children. They possess different personalities, desires and ways of understanding their surroundings, while the adults frequently fail because they attempt to impose straightforward categories upon something far more complicated. Although Sohn believes Korean schools are gradually changing and teachers are increasingly trying to understand students rather than merely control them, that older mentality remains visible."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Parents participate in the same system from another direction. Sohn does not believe the adults presented in “The Birds” simply do not care about their children, even when their behavior can appear apathetic. Instead, he points towards a tendency among Korean parents to entrust a very large part of their children’s education and daily development to schools."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The result can be a peculiar transfer of responsibility. Parents expect teachers and institutions to educate, supervise and solve problems, while teachers themselves are already overwhelmed by the demand to control large numbers of very different students. The apparent indifference visible in the film therefore emerges less from a complete absence of concern than from a system in which responsibility is continually being delegated."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The image of birds, however, predates almost every other aspect of the finished film. Sohn first conceived the basic idea approximately thirteen years ago while completing his mandatory military service. Frustrated by the restrictions of military life and facing a long period before his service would end, he watched birds simply fly across the boundary surrounding him."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "He remembers envying them. They could pass freely over the fences that contained him, producing the uncomplicated thought that he wanted to become a bird himself. That image eventually generated the earliest version of what would much later become “The Birds”."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The story at that stage was very different, but one central idea was already present: students would jump from a building after seeing birds. As Sohn continued thinking about the project over the following years, however, the symbolism gradually changed. Freedom and escape remained part of it, but birds increasingly came to represent something less reassuring."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "He began thinking about the unexpected misfortunes that enter people’s lives without warning. These events often seem impossible to identify beforehand, yet once they arrive they can completely alter everything around them. Sohn eventually transformed the birds into a metaphor for precisely that kind of invisible, unpredictable disaster."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "This idea is closely connected with Ye-ok’s personality. She attempts to understand the world through distinctions and classifications, much as the educational system categorizes students. If she can name something, separate it and place it within the right conceptual box, perhaps she can control it. The tragedy confronting her refuses to operate according to those rules."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The birds become the physical representation of something that may already be surrounding a person without being visible. Misfortune exists nearby, but it cannot necessarily be identified until the moment it suddenly arrives. “The Birds” thus turns a childhood-like fantasy of freedom into something far more unsettling: an image simultaneously associated with escaping confinement and confronting forces that cannot be understood."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Sohn also deliberately changed his approach to casting. On “That Summer’s Lie”, he had primarily searched for unknown performers and auditioned actors for practically every part. With his second feature, he wanted another kind of filmmaking experience and decided to work more extensively with established professional actors represented by agencies."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "His first meeting with Kang Kyung-heon, who plays Ye-ok, immediately reassured him about that decision. They spent a long time discussing the screenplay, and Sohn discovered that she had already been thinking deeply about its philosophical implications, including ideas connected with the “Butterfly Dream”. Their interpretations of the material connected quickly, making the first conversation unusually productive."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Other cast members were similarly attracted to the peculiar nature of the screenplay. Their professional experience allowed the production to progress differently from Sohn’s debut, where much of the process had involved finding performers without established screen personas. With “The Birds”, he was able to concentrate more directly on exploring the material with actors accustomed to the demands of a film set."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Post-production proved considerably more difficult. Sohn edited the movie himself and spent approximately a year and a half attempting to find its final form. The process involved repeatedly changing the structure and duration, making versions longer and shorter, abandoning particular approaches and occasionally stepping away from the edit entirely when exhaustion made it impossible to see the material clearly."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The visual effects made the process particularly challenging. Several sequences had to be assembled before the completed effects existed, forcing Sohn to imagine what elements would eventually appear within shots while simultaneously judging their rhythm. For a filmmaker coming from the comparatively stripped-down production of “That Summer’s Lie”, editing this type of material required learning an entirely different process."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "An even greater challenge was determining exactly what kind of film “The Birds” should become. Sohn knew that it needed to operate as a genre movie, and therefore required a certain rhythm and ability to sustain mystery. At the same time, he did not want the demands of genre to overwhelm his own filmmaking sensibility."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Much of the lengthy editing period was devoted to finding that middle ground. Too much emphasis on conventional genre mechanics risked producing a film that no longer felt like his own, while leaning completely into his previous style could undermine the increasingly strange narrative. The finished 139-minute version represents his attempt to retain both impulses."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "After such an exhausting post-production period, Sohn responded by doing something almost completely opposite. Rather than immediately trying to make another film on the expanded scale of “The Birds”, he has already shot his third feature with only a handful of actors."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "This time, he wanted to experience making a movie almost entirely alone. He operated the camera and recorded the sound himself, deliberately stripping away the larger crew that had enabled the ambitions of “The Birds”. The new project centers on actors and the question of creativity, although Sohn is not yet revealing many additional details."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The decision seems particularly fitting after a second feature defined by expansion. “The Birds” allowed Sohn to work with more people, experiment with genre, incorporate visual effects and spend a year and a half shaping a complicated narrative in the editing room. His next film appears to be an attempt to discover what happens when practically all of that infrastructure disappears."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "In that sense, Sohn’s early career already shows a filmmaker deliberately testing opposite methods rather than settling into one. “That Summer’s Lie” emerged from severe limitations, “The Birds” used increased resources to explore a much larger world, and the third feature now returns voluntarily to an almost solitary mode of production. What connects them is an interest in people who cannot quite understand one another, particularly adults and young people attempting to communicate across an increasingly difficult divide."}]
article_text:
Sohn Hyun-lok Talks “The Birds”, Korean Education, Invisible Misfortune and Finding Freedom in Flight

Sohn Hyun-lok discusses “The Birds”, Korean schools, generational conflict, the meaning of birds and his challenging 18-month edit.

Returning to the Busan International Film Festival has particular significance for Sohn Hyun-lok. Born and raised in the city, the filmmaker premiered his debut feature “That Summer’s Lie” in BIFF’s New Currents section in 2023, where it received the FIPRESCI Prize. Three years later, he returns with his second feature, “The Birds”, a considerably larger and more ambitious production that combines family drama, criticism of the Korean educational system and increasingly strange genre elements.

Speaking with Asian Movie Pulse in Busan, Sohn discussed the progression from his first feature, shifting the perspective from daughter to mother, his thoughts on Korean schools and parenting, the origins of the bird metaphor, working with professional actors, the lengthy editing process and the radically smaller project he has already shot as his third feature.

My Mother is screening at Busan International Film Festival

For Sohn, premiering two consecutive features at BIFF inevitably carries an emotional dimension beyond professional recognition. He was born and spent his adolescence in Busan, making the festival closely connected to his own personal history. Having both his debut and sophomore film introduced there consequently feels particularly meaningful, although the circumstances under which the two productions were made could hardly have been more different.

“That Summer’s Lie” was produced without significant financial support and with a crew of only around seven people. The limitations meant that Sohn had relatively few options regarding how the movie could be made. “The Birds”, by contrast, received funding and allowed him to work with a substantially larger group of technicians and actors. It remained a low-budget production, but the increase in resources gave him the opportunity to experiment with ideas that would simply have been impossible on his debut.

He hopes that difference is visible in the finished film. Rather than attempting to reproduce the intimacy and limitations of “That Summer’s Lie”, Sohn treated the second feature as an opportunity to discover what else his cinema could become. The larger ensemble, genre elements, visual effects and considerably broader narrative all emerged partly from that desire to try things he had not previously been able to attempt.

At the same time, the central character of “The Birds” developed directly from questions raised by his first film. “That Summer’s Lie” followed a teenage girl whose actions create increasing complications, but while making it Sohn began wondering about the mother on the opposite side of those conflicts. Why did the mother fail to understand what her daughter wanted? Why could two members of the same family look at the same situation and arrive at completely different interpretations?

“The Birds” reverses the viewpoint. Instead of remaining with the troubled daughter, Sohn wanted to follow a mother attempting to comprehend a child whose behavior increasingly escapes her understanding. Ye-ok’s position becomes even more complicated because she is simultaneously a parent and a teacher. At home she struggles with her own daughter, while at school she is professionally responsible for other people’s children.

This dual role also allowed Sohn to examine the way Korean adults look at young people. Although the behavior of some students in the movie can appear exceptionally harsh, he does not regard the film as an accusation against contemporary teenagers. Instead, he is more interested in the structures through which adults attempt to understand and control them.

In his view, the Korean school system has traditionally required teachers to manage students very strictly. One consequence is the temptation to classify children according to simple categories: those who study hard, those who do not, and those whose behavior adults find difficult to comprehend. Sohn wanted “The Birds” to push against precisely that way of thinking.

The students in the movie cannot be reduced to good and bad children. They possess different personalities, desires and ways of understanding their surroundings, while the adults frequently fail because they attempt to impose straightforward categories upon something far more complicated. Although Sohn believes Korean schools are gradually changing and teachers are increasingly trying to understand students rather than merely control them, that older mentality remains visible.

Parents participate in the same system from another direction. Sohn does not believe the adults presented in “The Birds” simply do not care about their children, even when their behavior can appear apathetic. Instead, he points towards a tendency among Korean parents to entrust a very large part of their children’s education and daily development to schools.

The result can be a peculiar transfer of responsibility. Parents expect teachers and institutions to educate, supervise and solve problems, while teachers themselves are already overwhelmed by the demand to control large numbers of very different students. The apparent indifference visible in the film therefore emerges less from a complete absence of concern than from a system in which responsibility is continually being delegated.

The image of birds, however, predates almost every other aspect of the finished film. Sohn first conceived the basic idea approximately thirteen years ago while completing his mandatory military service. Frustrated by the restrictions of military life and facing a long period before his service would end, he watched birds simply fly across the boundary surrounding him.

He remembers envying them. They could pass freely over the fences that contained him, producing the uncomplicated thought that he wanted to become a bird himself. That image eventually generated the earliest version of what would much later become “The Birds”.

The story at that stage was very different, but one central idea was already present: students would jump from a building after seeing birds. As Sohn continued thinking about the project over the following years, however, the symbolism gradually changed. Freedom and escape remained part of it, but birds increasingly came to represent something less reassuring.

He began thinking about the unexpected misfortunes that enter people’s lives without warning. These events often seem impossible to identify beforehand, yet once they arrive they can completely alter everything around them. Sohn eventually transformed the birds into a metaphor for precisely that kind of invisible, unpredictable disaster.

This idea is closely connected with Ye-ok’s personality. She attempts to understand the world through distinctions and classifications, much as the educational system categorizes students. If she can name something, separate it and place it within the right conceptual box, perhaps she can control it. The tragedy confronting her refuses to operate according to those rules.

The birds become the physical representation of something that may already be surrounding a person without being visible. Misfortune exists nearby, but it cannot necessarily be identified until the moment it suddenly arrives. “The Birds” thus turns a childhood-like fantasy of freedom into something far more unsettling: an image simultaneously associated with escaping confinement and confronting forces that cannot be understood.

Sohn also deliberately changed his approach to casting. On “That Summer’s Lie”, he had primarily searched for unknown performers and auditioned actors for practically every part. With his second feature, he wanted another kind of filmmaking experience and decided to work more extensively with established professional actors represented by agencies.

His first meeting with Kang Kyung-heon, who plays Ye-ok, immediately reassured him about that decision. They spent a long time discussing the screenplay, and Sohn discovered that she had already been thinking deeply about its philosophical implications, including ideas connected with the “Butterfly Dream”. Their interpretations of the material connected quickly, making the first conversation unusually productive.

Other cast members were similarly attracted to the peculiar nature of the screenplay. Their professional experience allowed the production to progress differently from Sohn’s debut, where much of the process had involved finding performers without established screen personas. With “The Birds”, he was able to concentrate more directly on exploring the material with actors accustomed to the demands of a film set.

Post-production proved considerably more difficult. Sohn edited the movie himself and spent approximately a year and a half attempting to find its final form. The process involved repeatedly changing the structure and duration, making versions longer and shorter, abandoning particular approaches and occasionally stepping away from the edit entirely when exhaustion made it impossible to see the material clearly.

The visual effects made the process particularly challenging. Several sequences had to be assembled before the completed effects existed, forcing Sohn to imagine what elements would eventually appear within shots while simultaneously judging their rhythm. For a filmmaker coming from the comparatively stripped-down production of “That Summer’s Lie”, editing this type of material required learning an entirely different process.

An even greater challenge was determining exactly what kind of film “The Birds” should become. Sohn knew that it needed to operate as a genre movie, and therefore required a certain rhythm and ability to sustain mystery. At the same time, he did not want the demands of genre to overwhelm his own filmmaking sensibility.

Much of the lengthy editing period was devoted to finding that middle ground. Too much emphasis on conventional genre mechanics risked producing a film that no longer felt like his own, while leaning completely into his previous style could undermine the increasingly strange narrative. The finished 139-minute version represents his attempt to retain both impulses.

After such an exhausting post-production period, Sohn responded by doing something almost completely opposite. Rather than immediately trying to make another film on the expanded scale of “The Birds”, he has already shot his third feature with only a handful of actors.

This time, he wanted to experience making a movie almost entirely alone. He operated the camera and recorded the sound himself, deliberately stripping away the larger crew that had enabled the ambitions of “The Birds”. The new project centers on actors and the question of creativity, although Sohn is not yet revealing many additional details.

The decision seems particularly fitting after a second feature defined by expansion. “The Birds” allowed Sohn to work with more people, experiment with genre, incorporate visual effects and spend a year and a half shaping a complicated narrative in the editing room. His next film appears to be an attempt to discover what happens when practically all of that infrastructure disappears.

In that sense, Sohn’s early career already shows a filmmaker deliberately testing opposite methods rather than settling into one. “That Summer’s Lie” emerged from severe limitations, “The Birds” used increased resources to explore a much larger world, and the third feature now returns voluntarily to an almost solitary mode of production. What connects them is an interest in people who cannot quite understand one another, particularly adults and young people attempting to communicate across an increasingly difficult divide.

article_text:
After eight years, Constance Wu is reuniting with the Young family for the Crazy Rich Asians HBO sequel series.

On Friday, the Golden Globe nominee teased the “really funny” script from the 2018 film’s co-writer Adele Lim, revealing the filming is taking place in New York City for the one-hour drama series, which got a series order from HBO earlier this month.

“Well, I mean, the first movie is based on the book by Kevin Kwan,” she explained on Today . “And he actually has a whole bunch of books in the Crazy Rich Asians world, and so a lot of it follows that. I could tell you that we’re all excited to be coming back. It’s filming here in New York where I live, so I’m thrilled about that. And I think it’s really funny.

Related Stories

‘Crazy Rich Asians’ Gets Series Order At HBO From Adele Lim, Jon M. Chu & Kevin Kwan

Jon M. Chu Shares ‘Crazy Rich Asians’ Series Update: “It’s A Real Thing”

Wu confirmed that production starts next year on the eight-episode series, and she’s read a script. “It’s very funny. I think it’s really good,” she said.

Watch on Deadline

“We’re in great hands because Adele is showrunning and writing and she did the original [film], and she’s just so smart and good and talented that I feel just great with her at the helm,” added Wu

Earlier this month, we reported that HBO gave the series a green light after about two years of development from Lim, the movie’s director Jon M. Chu, Nina Jacobson and Brad Simpson.

Wu is set to reprise her role Rachel Chu in the series, alongside Henry Golding as Nick Young and Ronny Chieng as Eddie Chang, with Michelle Yeoh recurring as Eleanor Sung-Young.

Weekly News Roundup: October 23, 2026

Art Basel Paris 2026 Closes Early Amid Widespread Unrest

Art Basel Paris will conclude its 2026 edition early at 7:00 PM on Friday, October 23, canceling its scheduled weekend public dates on October 24 and 25 amid escalating security concerns over nationwide student and civil unrest. The decision follows online calls from activist collectives urging demonstrations at the Grand Palais, the fair’s flagship venue. Tensions spilled into cultural spaces this week: student actions at the École du Louvre affected access to the museum, galleries such as Hauser & Wirth temporarily shut their doors, and the Jeu de Paume called off the opening reception for Stan Douglas’s survey exhibition. To secure Friday’s final hours, fair organizers deployed crash barriers outside the Grand Palais and instituted identity checks for entry. While ticket holders for the canceled weekend sessions are being contacted directly, fair management has not yet announced whether exhibitors will receive compensation or fee remissions.

ART SG Reveals Program Highlights for 2027 Edition

ART SG will return to the Marina Bay Sands Expo and Convention Centre from January 22–24, 2027, for its fifth edition, coinciding with Singapore Art Week. The fair will present an expanded slate of partnerships and programming, including an off-site, 11-day exhibition at 72-13 by Thai conceptual artist Pinaree Sanpitak, organized in collaboration with Sydney’s Artspace. Several initiatives will return, including the Singapore Art Museum’s acquisitive SGD 250,000 (USD 195,600) SAM ART SG Fund; the USD 10,000 ART SG FUTURES Prize, dedicated to an emerging artist showcased in the “FUTURES” sector; and the TVS Initiative for Indian and South Asian Contemporary Art, highlighting practitioners from the subcontinent. Co-located at Marina Bay Sands for a second consecutive year and curated by John Tung, SEA Focus will present its ninth edition under the theme “Better Worlds,” spotlighting artists and galleries from Southeast Asia. In a press release, ART SG co-founder Magnus Renfrew stated, “We look forward to welcoming the global art community back to Singapore this January, and to celebrating another chapter in the city’s vibrant contemporary art landscape.”

Tammy Nguyen to Present New Opera During Venice Biennale’s Closing Program

Vietnamese American artist Tammy Nguyen will present the prelude to her debut opera, Timaeus and The Teacher: Foreword, as part of the 61st Venice Biennale’s closing ceremonies from November 13–14. Commissioned and produced by Wesleyan University in Connecticut, the still-unfinished opera extends Nguyen’s long-running inquiry into ideologies of nationhood, collective memory, and the aftermath of the American war in Vietnam, drawing on her father’s experiences as a refugee. The aria, performed by Brian Vu, will center on an English teacher fleeing Saigon by boat and feature a tapestry of flags, building on works shown at Nguyen’s 2024–25 solo show at the Sarasota Art Museum in Florida. Speaking with The Art Newspaper , the artist said , “Before making the opera, I was trying to create a symphonic space, a holistic world where you can immerse yourself in the image and explore. All of that is still there, but now I want to have a psychological connection with the audience, through images that are ordinary, to talk about things that are extraordinary.”

Abu Dhabi Announces Plans for New Cultural District Ahead of the UAE’s First Frieze Fair

Ahead of the debut of Frieze Abu Dhabi, the government-owned developer Aldar announced plans for a new cultural district “Noma,” The Art Newspaper reports . The name is drawn from the site’s location to the north of Manarat Al Saadiyat. As Frieze Abu Dhabi’s official partner, Aldar made the announcement during Frieze London. Noma enters a crowded field of cultural districts that have taken shape within the Persian Gulf alongside the likes of the JAX district (Diriyah, Riyadh), Saadiyat Cultural District (Abu Dhabi), and Alserkal Avenue (Dubai). For now, the developer has yet to put forward any detailed plans for the project. The regional art market faces uncertainty amid the ongoing conflicts involving the US, Israel, Iran, and their allies, which has raised questions about the fair’s proceeding, a concern sharpened by the recent temporary shutdown of Saudi airspace after Houthi-led strikes on Riyadh International Airport. Nevertheless, Frieze signaled its intention to proceed with the Abu Dhabi edition.

What Does Loss Taste Like, curated by Chef Thomas Zacharias and The Locavore at the Serendipity Arts Festival in Goa, 2025. Courtesy Serendipity Arts.

Serendipity Arts Festival to Launch London Edition in November

Serendipity Arts, the Indian nonprofit behind Goa’s decade-old multidisciplinary arts festival, will debut an international edition in London from June 19–27, 2027. The nine-day program will showcase South Asian and diasporic practices across art, new media, dance, music, and culinary traditions. Staged alongside South Kensington’s annual Great Exhibition Road Festival, the event will activate local galleries, auditoriums, cafes, and public thoroughfares. An all-female curatorial cohort will direct the debut: Latika Gupta (visual art), Veeranganakumari Solanki and Nancy Adajania (new media), Sneha Khanwalkar (music), Preethi Athreya (dance), and Elizabeth Yorke (culinary arts). Participating institutions include the Victoria and Albert Museum, the Science Museum, the Natural History Museum, the Royal Albert Hall, the Royal College of Music, the Royal College of Art, and the Royal Geographical Society.

"paragraph", "text": "在入选的21部影片中，有19部是世界首映或国际首映，其中包括9部处女作长片。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在劳拉·贝穆德斯（Laura Bermúdez）和豪尔赫·加西亚（Jorge García）沉浸式且充满诗意的《Where the Sun Is Born》中，一名舞者离开洪都拉斯的城市，回到他年轻时生活的非裔加勒比加里富纳（Garifuna）社群——去寻找他的根和社群归属感。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "获得IDFA伯莎基金（IDFA Bertha Fund）支持的、由侯赛因·阿尔-阿萨迪（Hussein Al-asadi）执导的《She Was Not Alone》紧密记录了伊拉克南部沼泽地里一位与自然紧密相依的老年女性扎伊拉（Zaira）——沉思般地照亮了一个田园诗般却日益受到威胁的地方。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在IDFA项目空间NL（IDFA Project Space NL）校友拉鲁卡·卢帕斯库（Raluca Lupaşcu）的《A Modern Roma Fairytale》中，罗姆国王的10岁孙女尼科莱塔（Nicoleta）在一座大理石宫殿里梦想着生活——同时看着身边的女性在将塑造她未来的那些父权制传统的限制中艰难前行。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在《Every Death Diminishes Me》中，谢尔盖·巴热诺夫（Sergii Bazhenov）接受医务人员训练以加入前线，并记录了他的同事们救治伤员以及面对战争所带来的惨痛代价的过程。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "聚焦首映的 Frontlight 单元展映了 16 部电影，从“对真相及我们时代紧迫议题的批判性审视，到艺术家及其作品的肖像。”入选作品中有 15 部为世界首映或国际首映。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "IDFA 表示：“多部电影对重大的时事作出了直接回应，而另一些作品则留出时间进行反思，审视塑造人们生活的社会现实与挑战。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "加夫列尔·特赫多尔（Gabriel Tejedor）执导的《The Big Boom!》探讨了位于卡赞勒克的保加利亚武器制造商，其中充满矛盾与蓄势待发的紧张气氛，这里的机枪和火箭弹注定要运往乌克兰，而许多员工却支持普京。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在彼得·德尔普特（Peter Delpeut）和格尔科·德·雷伊特（Gerco de Ruijter）执导的《No Man’s Air》中，一名飞行员回忆了 1974 年 7 月飞往尼科西亚机场的最后一次航班，当时土耳其对塞浦路斯的入侵正迫在眉睫。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "阿夫萨内·萨拉里（Afsaneh Salari）的《Tehran, Under the Skin》走入德黑兰的美容诊所，探讨了伊朗为追求外表完美而广泛普及的整容文化背后的压力，并发生在一个试图控制女性美感的保守社会之中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在《Jenin & the Nakba Between Us》中，塞伦·胡斯尼（Serene Husni）回到了父母位于被占的约旦河西岸的家乡，将家族档案与同居民的对话交织在一起，勾勒出一处饱受流离失所、占领和记忆塑造的地方的肖像。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "节目增补周二公布的片单增补还包括了 Signed、Dead Angle: Common Ground、IDFA DocLab Spotlight、Best of Fests 以及 Special Screenings 选片。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Signed 单元近期新增的作品包括：亚历克斯·吉布尼（Alex Gibney）执导的《Musk》，这是一部剖析埃隆·马斯克权力和影响力的犀利之作；内森·菲尔德（Nathan Fielder）与兰斯·奥本海姆（Lance Oppenheim）执导的《You Can See Everything》，是一幅关于声名狼藉的 Theranos 创始人伊丽莎白·霍姆斯的复杂肖像；以及阿尔伯特·塞拉（Albert Serra）执导的《Sixteen Moments of My Life》，聚焦英格丽·卡文（Ingrid Caven）在巴黎北方剧院（Théâtre des Bouffes du Nord）的现场演唱。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Special Screenings 单元带来了由眼影电影博物馆（Eye Filmmuseum）修复的约翰·莱尔丹（John Leerdam）作品《30 mei, 1969 (gritu di un pueblo)》，该片重访了库拉索的历史性起义以及助长该起义的殖民不平等和种族歧视。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "IDFA DocLab Spotlight 单元公布了数部作品，包括达伦·爱默生（Darren Emerson）具有里程碑意义的 VR 体验作品《In Pursuit of Repetitive Beats》（IDFA，2022），该作品重访了英国 1980 年代后期的锐舞派对场景，并为 DocLab 20 周年推出了全新的集体多用户呈现形式。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "IDFA 沉浸式非虚构 DocLab 竞赛单元拥有 10 部作品，该竞赛单元大胆拓展了纪录片类型的视野，将沉浸式媒体推向传统边界之外。跨越 VR、现场戏剧表演、穹幕体验以及多感官作品，该单元的入选作品“探讨了沉浸式艺术如何改变我们遭遇现实的方式——提供意想不到的视角，并为能动性与抵抗开辟新的可能，”IDFA 表示。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "艺术节表示：“几位艺术家利用沉浸式体验，让观众与那些原本可能显得遥远的现实建立起亲密、具身的遭遇。其他作品则处理实体与身体，从数字方式改变我们对自身的感知、邀请我们的微生物享用盛宴，到通过放大所爱之人身体的腐烂来审视悲伤——将悲伤与死亡转化为深刻的反思，思考人类不过是更宏大生态系统的一部分。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "IDFA 数字叙事 DocLab 竞赛单元拥有 9 部作品，通过数字艺术、游戏、互动装置和现场表演拓展了纪录片的可能性。来自不同学科的艺术家让传统形式与新媒体展开对话，该单元展现了跨学科实验的新浪潮。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "IDFA 表示：“多部作品直面塑造当代生活的数字系统，颠覆算法并为人类的失误与能动性寻找空间。其他作品则邀请观众进入互动的开放世界，改编游戏与世界构建技术，创造出彻底偏离日常现实的参与式体验。在其他地方，艺术家探索实体与数字之间不断演变的关系统，调查技术如何根本性地塑造我们对亲密感、欲望和连接的体验。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "跨单元奖项 IDFA 还公布了跨单元奖项的提名名单——这些独特的奖项“超越了各个展映单元，旨在表彰整个艺术节节目中杰出的艺术成就。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "最佳长片处女作 IDFA 奖（IDFA Award for Best First Feature）“旨在表彰最卓越的长片处女作，认可那些展现出独特的创作声音和不断演进的个人风格之承诺的作品。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该奖项从国际竞赛、视野竞赛、Luminous 和 Frontlight 单元中选出，并伴随由国际评审团颁发的 5,000 欧元奖金。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "获得最佳长片处女作 IDFA 奖提名的电影，同时也具备角逐国际影评人费比西奖（FIPRESCI Award）的资格，该奖项由国际影评人评审团选出。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "最佳荷兰电影 IDFA 奖（IDFA Award for Best Dutch Film）旨在表彰国际竞赛、视野竞赛、Luminous 和 Frontlight 选片中杰出的荷兰电影制作才华。获奖电影人将获得由国际评审团颁发的 5,000 欧元奖金。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "最佳档案创意利用贝尔德与格鲁伊特 IDFA 重构奖（The Beeld & Geluid IDFA ReFrame Award for Best Creative Use of Archive）旨在表彰从整个电影节目中选出的杰出档案电影。获奖电影将获得由国际评审团颁发的 5,000 欧元奖金。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "获奖名单将于 11 月 19 日的 IDFA 颁奖典礼上公布。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
The International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam, the world’s leading documentary festival, has unveiled the main competition lineups for the 39th edition, which runs from Nov. 12 to 22. “White Tiger Column” opens the event, at which 253 titles from 80 countries will screen.

Newly unveiled selections include the International and Envision Competitions, Luminous, Frontlight and the IDFA DocLab competition selections, and the nominations for all cross-section awards.

Related Stories

Christy Carlson Romano Says Her Salary Was Half of Shia LaBeouf's on 'Even Stevens': 'We Were Co-Leads and Had the Same Screen Time'

Opening film IDFA opens with the world premiere of “White Tiger Column” by Robert Mentov, Dwight Jantzi and Bryan Dickie, following a group of recruits through 45 days of training with Myanmar ’s resistance movement. In a training camp deep in the jungle, the filmmakers capture the daily lives of young volunteers as they prepare to fight for their freedom.

Popular on Variety

“White Tiger Column” has been selected for the International Competition and nominated for the IDFA Award for Best First Feature.

International Competition The International Competition brings together works that “invite curiosity and critical reflection on our world today,” IDFA said. The selection of 13 titles brings together established veteran voices next to first-time filmmakers, with 12 films presenting their world or international premieres.

Bardi, dir. Tala Hadid (Morocco), 108’ – European Premiere

Crack in the Head, Crack in the Sky, dir. Mehran Tamadon (France), 120’ – World Premiere

Down the River, dir. Ruslan Fedotov (Germany), 79’ – World Premiere

Hazara Town, dir. Khadim Dai (Belgium/Australia/Germany), 103’ – World Premiere

Here Where the Fire Burns, dir. Juan Manuel Sepúlveda (Mexico), 97’ – World Premiere

An Incomplete Day in the History of Georgia 10.06.93, dir. Salomé Jashi (Georgia), 100’ – World Premiere

Lonan Tché, dir. Joël Richmond Mathieu Akafou (France/Italy/Ivory Coast/Senegal), 95’ – World Premiere

Mangabangabaka, dir. Michaël Andrianaly (France/Madagascar/Burkina Faso), 92’ – World Premiere

Morro Grande, dir. Isabel Joffily, Rita Toledo (Brazil/Netherlands), 88’ – World Premiere

Still Night, Burning House, dir. Carol Nguyen (Canada), 76’ – International Premiere

White Tiger Column, dir. Robert Mentov, Dwight Jantzi, Bryan Dickie (Canada), 95’ – World Premiere

Women and War, dir. Elwira Niewiera (Germany/Poland/Ukraine), 103’ – World Premiere

The Year of the Ghost, dir. Louis Hothothot (Netherlands/China), 95’ – World Premiere

Envision Competition The Envision Competition offers “13 unparalleled films, each of them stylistically arresting, as visionary filmmakers forge new cinematic languages,” the festival said.

“The selection brings together titles in which form drives the narrative. Through distinctive visual approaches and formal choices, the filmmakers deconstruct and reframe the complexities of our world, offering new ways of seeing and understanding the subjects they explore.”

Bahía Honda, dir. Alejandro Alonso Estrella (Cuba/France/Norway), 85’ – World Premiere

Between Revolutions, dir. Ruben Desiere (Belgium/Netherlands), 78’ – World Premiere

The Black Box Is Orange, dir. Yuula Benivolski (Canada), 89’ – International Premiere

Drop! Cover! Hold On!, dir. Stéphanie Roland (Belgium/France), 77’ – World Premiere

Lyrical Vengeance, dir. wendelien van oldenborgh (Netherlands), 111’ – World Premiere

Memories, dir. Anna Falguères (Belgium/France), 78’ – World Premiere

Memories of Lightning, dir. Riccardo Giacconi (France/Italy), 73’ – International Premiere

My Own Personal Gulag, dir. Lina Gorbaneva (Spain), 84’ – World Premiere

Radiant Mountain, dir. Miguel Moraes Cabral (Belgium/Portugal/France), 75’ – World Premiere

Ragazzi al fiume, dir. Pablo Briones (Switzerland), 75’ – World Premiere

Rivers of Memory, dir. Shishir Jha (India), 72’ – World Premiere

Vertigo Garden, dir. Lei Lei (Hong Kong / SAR /China), 73’ – World Premiere

You Don’t Die Two Times, dir. Ager Oueslati (Algeria/Germany/Netherlands), 90’ – World Premiere

Luminous The premiere-only section Luminous presents “a wide range of styles and formalist approaches, from observational to personal to experimental. Across both feature-length and short films, the titles grapple with big questions of life through deeply personal, lived experiences,” IDFA said.

Among the selection of 21 films, 19 titles are world or international premieres, including nine debut feature films.

In the immersive and poetic “Where the Sun Is Born” by Laura Bermúdez and Jorge García, a dancer leaves the city in Honduras to travel back to the Afro-Caribbean Garifuna community of his youth—in search of his roots and a sense of community.

The IDFA Bertha Fund-supported “She Was Not Alone” by Hussein Al-asadi closely follows Zaira, an elderly woman living in close communion with nature in the marshlands of southern Iraq—meditatively illuminating an idyllic place, increasingly under threat.

In the IDFA Project Space NL alumni Raluca Lupaşcu’s “A Modern Roma Fairytale,” 10-year-old Nicoleta, granddaughter of a Roma king, grows up dreaming of a life in a marble palace—while watching the women around her navigate the restrictions of the patriarchal traditions that will shape her future.

In “Every Death Diminishes Me,” Sergii Bazhenov trains as a medic to join the front lines, documenting his colleagues as they treat the wounded and confront the human cost of war.

Frontlight The premiere-only section Frontlight showcases 16 films, from “critically examinations of the truth and urgent issues of our time to portraits of artists and their work.” Fifteen of the selected titles are world or international premieres.

“Several films offer immediate responses to critical current events, while others take time to reflect, examining the social realities and challenges shaping people’s lives,” IDFA said.

“The Big Boom!” by Gabriel Tejedor explores a Bulgarian arms manufacturer in Kazanlak, rife with contradictions and simmering tension, where the machine guns and rockets are destined for Ukraine while many of its employees are pro-Putin.

In “No Man’s Air” by Peter Delpeut and Gerco de Ruijter, a pilot recalls the last flight to Nicosia Airport in July 1974, as a Turkish invasion of Cyprus loomed.

Afsaneh Salari’s “Tehran, Under the Skin” enters Tehran’s cosmetic clinics to explore the pressures behind Iran’s widespread culture of cosmetic surgery in pursuit of physical perfection, in a conservative society that seeks to control women’s beauty.

In “Jenin & the Nakba Between Us,” Serene Husni returns to her parents’ hometown in the occupied West Bank, weaving family archive and conversations with residents into a portrait of a place shaped by displacement, occupation and memory.

Additions to the program Tuesday’s program announcement also included additions to the Signed, Dead Angle: Common Ground, IDFA DocLab Spotlight, Best of Fests and Special Screenings selections.

Recent additions to Signed include Alex Gibney’s “Musk,” an incisive look at the power and influence of Elon Musk; Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s “You Can See Everything,” a complex portrait of notorious Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes; and “Sixteen Moments of My Life” by Albert Serra, spotlighting Ingrid Caven singing live at the Théâtre des Bouffes du Nord in Paris.

The Special Screenings section brings an Eye Filmmuseum restoration of John Leerdam’s “30 mei, 1969 (gritu di un pueblo),” that revisits the historic uprising in Curaçao and the colonial inequalities and racial discrimination that fuelled it.

The IDFA DocLab Spotlight selection announces several titles, including “In Pursuit of Repetitive Beats,” Darren Emerson’s landmark VR experience (IDFA, 2022) revisiting Britain’s late-1980s rave scene, presented in a new collective, multi-user format for DocLab’s 20th anniversary.

IDFA DocLab Competition for Immersive Non-Fiction With 10 titles, the IDFA DocLab Competition for Immersive Non-Fiction boldly expands the horizons of the documentary genre, pushing immersive media beyond conventional boundaries. Across VR, live theater performances, full-dome experiences, and multisensory works, the selection “explores how immersive art can alter the way we encounter reality—offering unexpected perspectives and opening up new possibilities for agency and resistance,” IDFA said.

“Several artists use immersive experiences to bring audiences into close, embodied encounters with realities that may otherwise feel distant. Other works deal with the corporeal and the body, from digitally altering our perception of ourselves and inviting our microbiomes to a feast, to examining grief through magnifying the decomposition of a loved one’s body—turning grief and death into a profound reflection on how humans are but a part of a larger ecosystem,” the festival said.

IDFA DocLab Competition for Digital Storytelling The nine-title IDFA DocLab Competition for Digital Storytelling expands the possibilities of documentary through digital art, games, interactive installations, and live performance. With artists from across disciplines bringing traditional forms into dialogue with new media, the selection showcases a new wave of cross-disciplinary experimentation.

“Several works confront the digital systems shaping contemporary life, subverting algorithms and finding room for human error and agency. Other works invite audiences into interactive open worlds, adapting game and world-building technologies to create participatory experiences that radically depart from everyday reality. Elsewhere, artists explore the ever-evolving relationship between the physical and digital, investigating how technology fundamentally shapes our experience of intimacy, desire, and connection,” IDFA said.

Cross-section awards IDFA has also announced the nominations for the cross-section awards—distinct awards that “transcend the program sections to recognize outstanding artistic achievement across the festival program.”

The IDFA Award for Best First Feature “celebrates the most remarkable debut feature-length films, recognizing works that reveal a distinctive creative voice and the promise of an evolving signature.”

Drawn from the International Competition, Envision Competition, Luminous and Frontlight, the award is accompanied by a €5,000 prize, awarded by an international jury.

The films nominated for the IDFA Award for Best First Feature are also eligible for the FIPRESCI Award, chosen by an international jury of film critics.

The IDFA Award for Best Dutch Film highlights exceptional Dutch filmmaking talent across the International Competition, Envision Competition, Luminous and Frontlight selections. The winning filmmaker with receive €5,000, awarded by an international jury.

The Beeld & Geluid IDFA ReFrame Award for Best Creative Use of Archive honors outstanding archival film, selected from across the film program. The winning film will receive a €5,000 prize, awarded by an international jury.

The winners will be announced during the IDFA awards ceremony on Nov. 19.

"他提出，自然是一个“政治、社会和学术张力的场域（……），一个充满现代废墟和后现代狂热的、处于争议中的象征空间”。许多著名的历史范例，如《船头草》杂志（Caballo de Proa）、《窗户》版画工坊（La Ventana）、库尔特伦出版社（Editorial Kultrún）、特里尔切（Trilce）和印第安（Índice）诗歌小组、阿道大学（UACh）造型艺术研究所、施温克与尼罗（Schwenke y Nilo）音乐二人组，以及那些曾活跃着加布里埃拉·古兹曼（Gabriela Guzmán）、豪尔赫·托雷斯（Jorge Torres）、卡洛斯·费舍尔（Carlos Fischer）、玛丽亚娜·马修斯（Mariana Mathews）、克莱门特·里德曼（Clemente Riedemann）、日耳曼·阿雷斯蒂萨巴尔（Germán Arestizábal）、维托尔·鲁伊斯·圣地亚哥（Víctor Ruiz Santiago）、马哈·比尔（Maha Vial）或里卡多·门多萨（Ricardo Mendoza）等众多名字的艺术节，都印证了一个强劲的文化传统，它在今天正寻找着新的河道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Apertura-residencia-Foto-Constanza-Rutherford.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "驻地项目开幕。摄影：康斯坦萨·拉瑟福德（Constanza Rutherford）", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "得益于艺术节，这份遗产与当下紧密相连。公共项目从阿道大学学生文化委员会（Comisión Cultural Estudiantil de la UACh）组织的艺术专业学生与毕业生见面会拉开帷幕。会上，几位毕业生试图根据她们的个人职业轨迹，阐明该领域的就业可能性。担任调解员、工艺工坊导师和文化管理者的经历比比皆是；大家坚持认为需要通过研究生学习继续深造并建立合作网络，但在空气中弥漫着一种悲观的情绪：在智利南部，大学毕业后很难继续致力于作品创作。这是一场为了靠艺术维生而经久不衰且令人身心俱疲的斗争。罗伯托·尼耶里（Roberto Nieri）在他的其中一张纸上写道：“什么是艺术？/ 艺术，就是冻得你直哆嗦 / 冰冷刺骨。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "与此同时，三个实验室召集了当地的艺术界。巴拉斯港绿色艺术节（Festival de Artes Verdes de Puerto Varas）总监康斯坦萨·盖尔（Constanza Güell）探讨了文化管理的新范式；“学校”平台（La Escuela）建筑师兼总监米格尔·布拉切利（Miguel Braceli）则带来了关于艺术与社群关系的国际视角；而伊格纳西奥·斯穆莱维奇（Ignacio Szmulewicz）在他的策展实验室中勾勒了艺术中展现的全球南方想象。他提及了面对迫在眉睫的气候危机时的末日美学、水作为入口的概念、河岸的隐喻、环境激进主义，以及远离首都从而得以打破中心、令南方艺术家在无数流派或当地常说的“无流派”杂糅中激荡。他暗指将南方视为待探索边境的旧有殖民想象，并让人想起1991年电影《嘶叫的石头》（Grito de piedra）中的维尔纳·赫尔佐格（Werner Herzog），其惊叹于巴塔哥尼亚未被驯服的自然，重现了崇高之物的浪漫主义理想。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Laboratorio-Arte-y-Comunidad.-Foto-Constanza-Rutherford.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "艺术与社群实验室。摄影：康斯坦萨·拉瑟福德（Constanza Rutherford）", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在巴尔迪维亚创作艺术，有可能不谈论自然吗？谈论自然，有可能不诉诸于智慧母亲的理想主义陈词滥调吗？我们有必要回想起赫尔佐格在纪录片《梦想的荷载》中，于亚马逊雨林深处拍摄《菲茨卡拉尔多》时的地狱般经历，当时他与自己疯狂的合作者兼敌人克劳斯·金斯基（Klaus Kinski）针锋相对：“金斯基总是说（雨林）充满了色情元素。而我看到的更多是猥亵。我看到的是交媾、窒息、生存之争，以及单纯的腐烂。这里的自然是卑劣而低下的。鸟儿不唱歌，它们在痛苦中尖叫。相比之下，我们听起来就像是出自愚蠢的廉价市郊小说中的那些发音不准、半生不熟的短句。甚至连天上的繁星，在这里看起来也像是一场混乱。我们不得不习惯这样一种观点：宇宙中并不存在我们所构想的那种和谐。但当我这样说时，我对雨林充满了钦佩。我并不是恨它。我非常爱它。但我爱它是违背我最好判断的。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "南方还是非南方，这是一个问题。在追寻情感与社群的过程中，绝不能忽视当代艺术令人不安、产生碰撞并揭示分歧的巨大潜力。危险在于，一如既往的圈子将自己封闭起来，在于巴尔迪维亚的艺术无法从大学走入同样构成该地区的街区和各个市镇，在于当代艺术依然是一个泡沫，少数人聚在里面与那些和他们想法一致的人交谈。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Encuentro-¿que-Bienal-sonamos-Foto-Constanza-Rutherford.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "“我们为地区艺坛梦想着怎样的双年展？”座谈会。摄影：康斯坦萨·拉瑟福德（Constanza Rutherford）", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在10月6日星期二的闭幕活动期间，展出了基于“水/天空：世界之门”（Agua/Cielo: Portales de mundo）驻留项目创作的作品。该项目于今年9月初举行，由“大海深处基金会”（Fundación Mar Adentro）内容总监玛雅·埃拉苏里斯（Maya Errázuriz）策展。水面上绘制的文字、水坑回路、基于河流形状的字体以及勾勒记忆的小麦谷物，为该艺术节的第二届铺平了道路。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "几天前的10月4日星期六，另一幅长卷在拉列涅拉文化中心（Centro Cultural La Leñera）展开。在长卷中，参与者被邀请回答“我们为地区艺坛梦想着怎样的双年展？”这一问题。巴尔迪维亚当代艺术博物馆（Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Valdivia）这座白象般的建筑如幽默般在对话中徘徊，伴随着一个世界级展览空间的承诺，却一再延迟。巴尔迪维亚在后自然哲学时代成为艺术思想焦点的潜力变得显而易见。最后的声音似乎齐声交织在一起：巴尔迪维亚配得上一个当代艺术双年展。", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "heading", "text": "El paisaje fluvial y la exuberancia natural de Valdivia definen buena parte de su producción artística, pero también abren preguntas sobre los límites y las posibilidades de una escena cultural que busca proyectarse más allá de sus fronteras. A propósito de su primera edición, el Festival de Arte Contemporáneo de la ciudad ofrece una ocasión para mirar sus tradiciones, reconocer nuevas prácticas y preguntarse qué futuro colectivo puede imaginar el arte desde el sur."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "La obsesión valdiviana por la naturaleza es inevitable. Los arbustos se asoman entre el cemento, los edificios no pueden superar cierta altura porque el suelo se hunde en humedales, y basta caminar unos pocos minutos en cualquier dirección para encontrarse con la frondosa selva que envuelve la vista con su asombrosa biodiversidad. Frente a los nueve metros cuadrados de área verde por persona que recomienda la Organización Mundial de la Salud para las ciudades, en Valdivia se superan los 19 metros cuadrados por persona. Pero los datos duros no expresan la fuerza ontológica con que el paisaje natural afecta a quienes habitan su territorio. Para eso es mejor el arte."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Ya lo decía la recientemente premiada autora Nina Avellaneda en una entrevista para la revista Los libros después de la peste : “En Valdivia las personas no son protagónicas, los árboles y los ríos son más ciudad que las personas. El paisaje se lo come todo”. Ese paisaje es también el punto de partida del 1er Festival de Arte Contemporáneo de la ciudad, realizado entre el 29 de septiembre y el 6 de octubre, nacido al alero del Programa Los Ríos Territorio Visual —impulsado por la Seremi de las Culturas, las Artes y el Patrimonio —, que a lo largo de siete años ha fortalecido las artes visuales en la Región de Los Ríos."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "La pequeña urbe del sur de Chile pareciera tener una tendencia a los festivales. Sus circuitos de puentes, costaneras, ferias fluviales, ríos y parques son una geografía ideal para recorridos y un ambiente que estimula la colectividad, el intercambio de ideas y el tan preciado networking . A lo largo de las distintas exposiciones, laboratorios curatoriales, mesas de trabajo, charlas y presentaciones de libros, las caras se repiten."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Naturaleza y más naturaleza. La exposición central del festival, curada por Ignacio Szmulewicz y Gabriela Urrutia , presenta cuatro obras basadas en la experiencia de la residencia Cuencas , en la cual, durante una semana de la primavera del 2025, artistas y curadores recorrieron el río Valdivia desde su nacimiento en la cordillera hasta su desembocadura en el mar. Mediante visitas a archivos, museos y centro culturales, y conversaciones con comunidades y expertos, los residentes pudieron empaparse de la naturaleza del territorio. Los resultados se exhiben en cuatro puntos del campus de los museos de la Universidad Austral de Chile (UACh) ."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Roberto-Nieri-Bitacora-de-viaje-Foto-Constanza-Rutherford.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Roberto Nieri, Bitácora de viaje , 2026. La obra resuena con el mítico rollo de Jack Kerouac , en el que escribió la primera versión de su clásica novela On the road publicada en 1957: 36 metros de papel que facilitaron su prosa espontánea, sin pausas, inspirada en el flujo de conciencia continuo de los viajes."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Resuena también con El rollo de Chile Chico (2004) del escritor valdiviano Pedro Guillermo Jara (1951-2019), donde este aprovechaba la forma de los rollos bíblicos del Mar Muerto para fantasear sobre el pasado y el futuro de la Patagonia y sus habitantes. Tiene sentido que a Roberto Nieri le guste entender su obra Bitácora de viaje como una especie de publicación alternativa, un libro de artista que se extiende por las alturas y extremidades de la sala."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Jose-Martinez-Vestigios-de-la-ribera.-Foto-Fabiola-Pontigo.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "José Martínez, Vestigios de la ribera , 2026. article_text:
El paisaje fluvial y la exuberancia natural de Valdivia definen buena parte de su producción artística, pero también abren preguntas sobre los límites y las posibilidades de una escena cultural que busca proyectarse más allá de sus fronteras. A propósito de su primera edición, el Festival de Arte Contemporáneo de la ciudad ofrece una ocasión para mirar sus tradiciones, reconocer nuevas prácticas y preguntarse qué futuro colectivo puede imaginar el arte desde el sur.

La obsesión valdiviana por la naturaleza es inevitable. Los arbustos se asoman entre el cemento, los edificios no pueden superar cierta altura porque el suelo se hunde en humedales, y basta caminar unos pocos minutos en cualquier dirección para encontrarse con la frondosa selva que envuelve la vista con su asombrosa biodiversidad. Frente a los nueve metros cuadrados de área verde por persona que recomienda la Organización Mundial de la Salud para las ciudades, en Valdivia se superan los 19 metros cuadrados por persona. Pero los datos duros no expresan la fuerza ontológica con que el paisaje natural afecta a quienes habitan su territorio. Para eso es mejor el arte.

Ya lo decía la recientemente premiada autora Nina Avellaneda en una entrevista para la revista Los libros después de la peste : “En Valdivia las personas no son protagónicas, los árboles y los ríos son más ciudad que las personas. El paisaje se lo come todo”. Ese paisaje es también el punto de partida del 1er Festival de Arte Contemporáneo de la ciudad, realizado entre el 29 de septiembre y el 6 de octubre, nacido al alero del Programa Los Ríos Territorio Visual —impulsado por la Seremi de las Culturas, las Artes y el Patrimonio —, que a lo largo de siete años ha fortalecido las artes visuales en la Región de Los Ríos.

La pequeña urbe del sur de Chile pareciera tener una tendencia a los festivales. Sus circuitos de puentes, costaneras, ferias fluviales, ríos y parques son una geografía ideal para recorridos y un ambiente que estimula la colectividad, el intercambio de ideas y el tan preciado networking . A lo largo de las distintas exposiciones, laboratorios curatoriales, mesas de trabajo, charlas y presentaciones de libros, las caras se repiten.

Naturaleza y más naturaleza. La exposición central del festival, curada por Ignacio Szmulewicz y Gabriela Urrutia , presenta cuatro obras basadas en la experiencia de la residencia Cuencas , en la cual, durante una semana de la primavera del 2025, artistas y curadores recorrieron el río Valdivia desde su nacimiento en la cordillera hasta su desembocadura en el mar. Mediante visitas a archivos, museos y centro culturales, y conversaciones con comunidades y expertos, los residentes pudieron empaparse de la naturaleza del territorio. Los resultados se exhiben en cuatro puntos del campus de los museos de la Universidad Austral de Chile (UACh) .

En la Galería Réplica , Roberto Nieri (1986), periodista, documentalista y poeta, imita la línea descendiente del río (o quizás las curvas de las montañas) a través de un largo pliego donde distintos dibujos, acuarelas y escritos resaltan momentos, pensamientos y sensaciones de la deriva fluvial. La obra resuena con el mítico rollo de Jack Kerouac , en el que escribió la primera versión de su clásica novela On the road publicada en 1957: 36 metros de papel que facilitaron su prosa espontánea, sin pausas, inspirada en el flujo de conciencia continuo de los viajes.

Resuena también con El rollo de Chile Chico (2004) del escritor valdiviano Pedro Guillermo Jara (1951-2019), donde este aprovechaba la forma de los rollos bíblicos del Mar Muerto para fantasear sobre el pasado y el futuro de la Patagonia y sus habitantes. Tiene sentido que a Roberto Nieri le guste entender su obra Bitácora de viaje como una especie de publicación alternativa, un libro de artista que se extiende por las alturas y extremidades de la sala.

La casona donde hoy funciona el Museo de la Exploración Rudolph Amandus Philippi de la UACh fue trasladada de su locación original entre 2005 y 2006, mediante el desarme de 80 mil piezas que luego se reconstruyeron como un rompecabezas gigante en su ubicación actual. José Martínez (1996), artista, performer y poeta, refleja esta hazaña con su obra Vestigios de la ribera , donde dispone 80 tablas con la forma de la planta de una de las clásicas cabañas de vivienda social del barrio de la Teja obrera, con un imponente nido al centro como símbolo del hogar.

El régimen de verdad del museo aparece deconstruido por la memoria doméstica presente en la madera, donde ha inscrito diversas palabras con pirografía: polillas, pieza, tarro de leche, lluvia, autitos, embarazo, allegados, ventana, fracasos, velador, cajones, hambre, borracho.

Al interior del Museo Histórico Antropológico Maurice Van de Maele , la artista multimedial y poeta María Hurtado (1992) ha montado Ser puente , el punto alto de la exhibición principal. De un lado se muestran fotografías de la residencia capturadas a través de una cámara oscura estenopeica artesanal, tecnología precursora de la fotografía, que demuestra ser ideal para evocar los espíritus del paisaje austral. Lejos del registro documental exacto o en alta definición, las imágenes del río aparecen cubiertas por una atmósfera fantasmagórica y onírica, que se acerca al territorio desde abstracciones sensibles.

Del otro lado de la sala, en un contraste radical, la artista invita a conversar por chat con una inteligencia artificial que encarna la voz del río, basada en 38 entrevistas a personas vinculadas a distintos puntos de la cuenca. El río habla como una voz colectiva, una entidad viva y relacional hecha de relatos, memorias e imaginaciones poéticas. La naturaleza sirve de excusa para explorar las amplitudes de la historia de la tecnología.

Finalmente, en el Centro Cultural La Leñera , la diseñadora y artista Constanza Garrido (1986) ha montado una carpa traslúcida hecha de múltiples bolsitas plásticas donde 200 niños y jóvenes fueron guardando objetos pequeños recogidos a orillas del río, guiados por los elementos de agua, aire, fuego y tierra. Hojas, pedazos de telas, plásticos y basuritas de diversos colores conforman un gabinete de curiosidades que muestra las distintas formas que acompañan al río y que, en conjunto, constituyen una obra de autoría colectiva, reforzando la idea del río como gatillador de relaciones.

Los valdivianos están enamorados de Valdivia. Durante el año 2024, el historiador del arte Ignacio Szmulewicz curó la exposición Santuario en el Centro Cultural Palacio Pereira , ubicado en pleno centro de la capital chilena, una retrospectiva del arte contemporáneo en Valdivia desde los años 80 hasta la actualidad. En ella, proponía pensar sus múltiples formas a partir de la oficialización, en 1981, del ecosistema de humedales formado tras el terremoto de 1960 como santuario de la naturaleza.

La naturaleza, planteaba, es un “campo de tensiones políticas, sociales y académicas (…), un espacio simbólico en disputa, plagado de ruinas modernas y delirios posmodernos”. Notables ejemplos históricos como la revista Caballo de Proa , el taller de grabado La Ventana , la editorial Kultrún, los grupos de poesía Trilce e Índice , el Instituto de Artes Plásticas de la UACh, el dúo musical Schwenke y Nilo, los festivales artísticos por donde circulaban nombres como Gabriela Guzmán, Jorge Torres, Carlos Fischer, Mariana Mathews, Clemente Riedemann, Germán Arestizábal, Víctor Ruiz Santiago, Maha Vial o Ricardo Mendoza, entre muchos otros, dan cuenta de una potente tradición cultural que hoy encuentra nuevos cauces.

Gracias al Festival, ese legado se conecta con el presente. El Programa Público comienza con el encuentro de estudiantes y egresados de artes organizado por la Comisión Cultural Estudiantil de la UACh. En ella, distintas egresadas intentan dar luces, a partir de sus trayectorias personales, sobre las posibilidades laborales del área. Abundan las experiencias como mediadoras, talleristas de oficios y gestoras culturales; se insiste en la necesidad de continuar especializándose con estudios de posgrado y de generar redes de colaboración, pero queda en el aire una sensación pesimista de que, en el sur de Chile, cuesta seguir dedicándose a producir obras después de egresar de la universidad. La vieja lucha desgastante por vivir del arte. Roberto Nieri escribe en una de sus hojas: “¿Qué es el arte? / El arte, cagarte de frío / Helarte”.

En paralelo, tres laboratorios convocan a la comunidad artística local. Constanza Güell , directora del Festival de Artes Verdes de Puerto Varas , explora los nuevos paradigmas de la gestión cultural; Miguel Braceli , arquitecto y director de la plataforma La Escuela , suma perspectivas internacionales sobre las relaciones entre arte y comunidad; mientras Ignacio Szmulewicz esboza en su laboratorio curatorial las imaginaciones del sur del mundo presentes en el arte. Menciona las estéticas del fin ante la inminente crisis climática, la idea del agua como un portal, la metáfora de la orilla, el activismo medioambiental y la lejanía de la capital que permite perder el centro y revuelve a los artistas del sur en infinitas mezclas de disciplinas o, como suelen decir en la zona, indisciplinas. Alude a los viejos imaginarios coloniales que veían el sur como una frontera a explorar. Recuerda al Werner Herzog de la cinta Grito de piedra de 1991, maravillado por la naturaleza indómita de la Patagonia, repitiendo los ideales románticos de lo sublime.

¿Es posible hacer arte en Valdivia sin hablar de naturaleza? ¿Es posible hablar de naturaleza sin recurrir a los clichés idealistas de la madre sabia ante la cual debemos agacharnos humildemente para aprender? Vale la pena recordar también al Herzog del documental Burden of dreams , durante la infernal filmación de Fitzcarraldo en la profundidad de la selva amazónica, cuando antagonizaba con su delirante colaborador y enemigo Klaus Kinski: “Kinski siempre dice que [la selva] está llena de elementos eróticos. Yo la veo más bien llena de obscenidad. Veo fornicación, asfixia, luchas por sobrevivir y simplemente pudrirse. La naturaleza acá es vil y baja. Los pájaros no cantan, chillan de dolor. Y nosotros, en comparación, solo sonamos como frases mal pronunciadas y a medio terminar, sacadas de una estúpida novela barata suburbana. Incluso las estrellas aquí arriba, en el cielo, parecen un desorden. Tenemos que acostumbrarnos a la idea de que no hay armonía en el universo, tal como la hemos concebido. Pero cuando digo esto, lo digo con total admiración por la selva. No es que la odie. La amo muchísimo. Pero la amo en contra de mi mejor juicio”.

Sur o no sur, esa es la cuestión. En la búsqueda de afectividades y comunidad, no se debe dejar de lado el inmenso potencial del arte contemporáneo para incomodar, generar choques y revelar desacuerdos. El peligro está en que los mismos círculos de siempre se cierren sobre sí mismos, en que el arte valdiviano no pueda salir de la Universidad hacia los barrios y las diversas comunas que también constituyen la región, en que el arte contemporáneo persista en ser una burbuja donde unos pocos se reúnen a conversar con gente que piensa igual que ellos.

Durante las actividades de cierre, el martes 6 de octubre, se exhibieron obras basadas en la residencia Agua/Cielo: Portales de mundo , realizada a inicios de septiembre de este año y curada por la directora de contenidos de la Fundación Mar Adentro , Maya Errázuriz . Palabras dibujadas sobre agua, circuitos de pozas, tipografías basadas en las formas del río y cereales de trigo que cartografían recuerdos abren el paso a la segunda versión del festival.

Días antes, el sábado 4 de octubre, otro rollo se extendía en el Centro Cultural La Leñera. En él, se invitó a los participantes a responder a la pregunta “¿qué bienal soñamos para el futuro de la escena regional?”. El elefante blanco del Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Valdivia ronda como un fantasma por las conversaciones, con la promesa de un espacio expositivo de talla mundial que insiste en retrasarse. El potencial de Valdivia para perfilarse como un foco de pensamiento artístico en época de filosofías post naturales se hace evidente. Las voces finales parecen mezclarse al unísono: Valdivia se merece una Bienal de Arte Contemporáneo.

article_text:
It’s another milestone for “The History of Concrete.” The off-beat documentary about… well, the title says it all, has crossed the $2 million mark 25 days into its run. That’s a strong result for a non-fiction film , as well as a testament to the appeal of its director John Wilson , who has built a passionate following thanks to his cult favorite HBO series “How To with John Wilson.”

Magnolia, the indie studio behind the documentary, picked up the film at this year’s Sundance Film Festival, where it was a hit with critics . The total gross now stands at $2,042,000. “ The History of Concrete ” is currently playing on 172 screens in North America, which includes 11 screens in Canada. It will shed some venues this weekend, dropping to 125 screens.

The film, which touches on issues of urbanism and architecture with Wilson’s absurdist flair , has been a huge hit at the IFC Center, surpassing $300,000, making it one of the indie theater’s highest-grossing titles ever.

“‘The History of Concrete’ has worked in every market we’ve opened,” said Neal Block, Magnolia’s head of distribution and marketing. “I don’t think in my 20 years at Magnolia that I’ve ever received more emails from exhibitors expressing delight at how a film is performing, and asking to book return engagements and encore screenings. It’s not playing like a documentary; it’s not playing like a comedy — it’s sort of charting its own path theatrically, since it’s very much its own singular piece of art.”

“The History of Concrete” also picked up four Critic’s Choice nominations this week , including nods for best documentary feature and best first documentary feature. It was also nominated for its editing and narration.
